item.title: About BFMG
item.dc:creator: aa3025
item.content:encoded:
We are academics at the University of Coventry, and enthusiastic about mathematical games! These are widespread in other countries, with tens of thousands of participants every year. The first edition of the British Final took place at the University of Essex, in 2022, and the second edition at the University of Coventry, in 2023. Last year, for the first time British participants qualified for the International Final! Our long term goal is to broaden interest for the games in the UK across schools, universities, and the general public. In general, no specialist knowledge is required to solve, but a lot of creativity will certainly help!   Who can take part in Logic & Mathematical Games? -- Everyone! You can participate in one of these categories: Categories:
CHILDREN
  • CE    Year 5 students     5 problems, max. 60 minutes
  • CM    Year 6-7 students     8 problems, max. 90 minutes
  • C1    Year 8-9 students     11 problems, max. 120 minutes
  • C2    Year 10-11 students     14 problems, max. 180 minutes
TEENS AND SCHOLARS
  • L1    Post-mandatory school students     16 problems, max. 180 minutes
  • L2    University students     18 problems, max. 180 minutes
ADULTS
  • GP    Adults, general public     16 problems, max. 180 minutes
  • HC    Adults, top-level competition     18 problems, max. 180 minutes
  Rules: For ranking purposes, in each category, in order or priority:
  • 1) most correctly solved problems;
  • 2) if tied, most points;
  • 3) if still tied, least time;
  • 4) if still tied, youngest participant first.
No calculators, computers, phones, etc. Allowed material: pens, pencils, erasers, rulers, protractors, compasses, scissors.   Contact BFMG     Useful links for past editions, trainings:
  • 2024-25 Semi-final paper: https://www.fsjm.ch/static/archives/39_20_CH_en_questions.pdf
  • 2022_final

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: aa3025
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: https://bfmg.maths.coventry.domains.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.content:encoded:
The 2024 final of the Logic and Mathematical Games will take place on the campus of Coventry University, CV1 2JH, on Saturday, 25th May 2024, from 1pm to 4pm (time and number of problems vary by category).

The schedule for May 25th is:
11:00-12:45 arrival, registration;
13:00-16:00 competitions;
from 17:00 or 17:30 rankings, closing ceremony.
Can you solve these questions and puzzles?  

Participants around the world scoring high enough will qualify for the International Final, at its 38th edition in 2024, to be held on 25-26 August in Paris, France!

To participate register here: https://forms.office.com/e/GxAwfTLwBu

For further information contact us here: https://forms.office.com/e/6XyWriHgHT

We also organise weekly logic and math problem solving sessions at Coventry Uni. These are informal, if you would like to participate let us know at the above address.

We look forward to seeing you!

item.title: 2025 International Final of 39 Mathematical Games in Tunisia, Mahdia, 21-25 August 2025
item.dc:creator: aa3025
item.content:encoded:
Dear All The International Final will take place on Saturday, August 23rd and Sunday, August 24th, 2025, in the city of Mahdia, Tunisia at the Faculty of Economics and Management of Mahdia. Mahdia is a coastal city located 208 km from the capital Tunis (which has the Tunis-Carthage International Airport) and 40 km from the city of Monastir (which has the Habib Bourguiba International Airport). The Local Organising Committee (LOC) has scheduled to welcome participants starting from Thursday, August 21st, and departures are planned for Monday, August 25th, 2025.

Relevant Information:

  • The Programme of the events:  Programme 39 eme finale JM, english version: Programme
  • A variety of accommodation options in Mahdia for the period of August 21st to 25th (after contacting residences and hotels for reservations) --> please fill in Reservation column and email back to us, here is English version: Accomoodations JM 26 Mai 2025
  • Fill in the participants and accomp. persons list here: Fiche_Participant 39eme JM (ENG)
Participation fees
  • Registration fee: 15 EUR
  • Meal of the 2nd day for participants: 5 EUR
  • Meal of the 2nd day for the Companions: 8 EUR
  • Tours on Friday are free

item.title: Outstanding Achievements for Team GB at the International Mathematical Games 2026 Final in Milan!
item.dc:creator: aa3025
item.content:encoded:
We are thrilled to share the fantastic results of  🇬🇧Team GB 🇬🇧 at the 2-day International Mathematical  and Logical Games Final, held in Bocconi University (Italy, Milan) on 25-26 July, 2026! Competing against top mathematical talent from around the globe, our team delivered exceptional performances across multiple categories, bringing home two 1st place champion titles and several top-10 finishes.

Highlights & Individual Standings

CE// Category (Parallel)

  • Samuel Stuart took 1st Place in the world with a score of 10 solved puzzles in just 43 minutes!
  • Yison Li delivered a strong performance, finishing in 5th Place (8 solved)!

CM Category

  • Monica Stuart earned an impressive 10th Place finish in competitive 63-contestants group, solving 15 puzzles!

C1 Category

  • Yusuf Shah secured 1st Place globally amongst 88 contestants with a maximum score of 22 solved puzzles in amazing 120 minutes!

C1// Category (Parallel)

  • Solomon Stuart placed 4th with 21 solved puzzles in 130 minutes!.

L1 Category

  • Anoushka Bouri placed 38th in a highly competitive division, solving 24 puzzles!

L2// Category (Parallel)

  • Josh Turley achieved a fantastic 7th Place finish with 27 solved puzzles!

GP// Category (Parallel)

  • Rico Li represented GB in the General Public parallel category, placing 19th with 23 solved puzzles!
A huge congratulations  🎉 to all our finalists for their incredible logic, speed, and dedication on the international stage! UK Participants:UK Participants with support Team:
